Good morning. It's Thursday, August 13. Here's your pre-market briefing.

Three things stand out this morning. First, the S&P 500 closed at 7,748.50, up
0.26%, and is now up 13.2% on the year. Second, the long end of the curve is
doing the work, with the ten-year at 4.68%. Third, the thirty-year auction
lands this afternoon.

Turning to the overnight tape. The Nasdaq Composite finished at 26,588.49, up
0.54%, and the Russell 2000 added 0.61%. In Asia, the Nikkei gained 1.63%.
Volatility stayed contained, with the VIX at 14.55, down 4.8% on the session,
against a twenty-day average of 17.0. Three-month volatility sits at 18.53, so
the curve is still in contango.

On rates. The two-year sits at 4.20%, down 2 basis points. The ten-year is at
4.68%, also down 2 basis points. That leaves the two-year to ten-year spread at
48 basis points. Consumer prices are running at 3.3% year over year.

On the corporate side. Super Micro Computer led the tape, up 19.0% to $37.61 on
3.3x average volume. Uber lagged, down 4.0% to $75.36. Technology was the
strongest sector, up 1.49%. Gold settled at 4,465.90.

Looking ahead. Treasury sells $25 billion of thirty-year paper at 1:00 p.m.

That's your briefing. Have a good one.
